474	def _merge_node(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
475	    """Fold two schema nodes over disjoint batches into one new node."""
476	    kind = left["kind"]
477	    if kind == "object":
478	        if _is_collapsed(left) or _is_collapsed(right):
479	            # One side gave up per-field detail, so the union can only be
480	            # reported as a collapsed, marked summary.
481	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
482	            node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
483	            return node
484	        node = _new_node("object")
485	        node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
486	        left_overflow = left.get("overflow")
487	        right_overflow = right.get("overflow")
488	        names = list(left["fields"]) + [
489	            name for name in right["fields"] if name not in left["fields"]
490	        ]
491	        for name in names:
492	            le = left["fields"].get(name)
493	            re = right["fields"].get(name)
494	            if le is None:
495	                # The field is missing on the left; if the left capped its
496	                # fields, its occurrences of this field landed in the left
497	                # overflow entry, so the merged entry must absorb them and
498	                # be marked approximate. That field's own occurrences on
499	                # the right prove its name is folded too.
500	                if left_overflow is not None:
501	                    entry = _merge_field(left_overflow, re)
502	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
503	                    entry["approximate"] = True
504	                else:
505	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(re)
506	            elif re is None:
507	                if right_overflow is not None:
508	                    entry = _merge_field(le, right_overflow)
509	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
510	                    entry["approximate"] = True
511	                else:
512	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(le)
513	            else:
514	                entry = _merge_field(le, re)
515	            node["fields"][name] = entry
516	        if left_overflow is not None or right_overflow is not None:
517	            if left_overflow is None:
518	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(right_overflow)
519	            elif right_overflow is None:
520	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(left_overflow)
521	            else:
522	                overflow = _merge_field(left_overflow, right_overflow)
523	            overflow["approximate"] = True
524	            node["overflow"] = overflow
525	        return node
526	    if kind == "array":
527	        node = _new_node("array")
528	        if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):
529	            node["approximate"] = True
530	        kinds = list(left["elements"]) + [
531	            element_kind
532	            for element_kind in right["elements"]
533	            if element_kind not in left["elements"]
534	        ]
535	        for element_kind in kinds:
536	            lc = left["elements"].get(element_kind)
537	            rc = right["elements"].get(element_kind)
538	            if lc is None:
539	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(rc)
540	            elif rc is None:
541	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(lc)
542	            else:
543	                node["elements"][element_kind] = _merge_node(lc, rc)
544	        return node
545	    return _new_node(kind)

548	def _merge_field(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
549	    """Fold two field entries over disjoint batches into one new entry."""
550	    entry = _new_field()

552	    if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):

574	def _subtract_node(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
575	    """Return the part of ``mem`` folded after ``base`` was taken."""
576	    kind = mem["kind"]
577	    if kind == "object":
578	        if _is_collapsed(mem):

589	            else:

596	            else:

604	        for element_kind, child in mem["elements"].items():
605	            base_child = base_elements.get(element_kind)
606	            if base_child is None:

608	            else:

614	def _subtract_field(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
615	    entry = _new_field()

617	    if mem.get("approximate"):
618	        entry["approximate"] = True

620	    if mem_names is not None:
621	        # The delta cannot attribute provenance per name (only aggregate
622	        # counts are kept), so it carries every name its memory ever folded

624	        # only ever widens validation for genuinely folded names.

627	        base_child = base["types"].get(kind)
628	        if base_child is None:

630	        else:

638	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.
639	    if name.isidentifier():

641	    return f"{path}[{json.dumps(name)}]"

648	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;

654	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:

657	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
658	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
659	        return
660	    fields = node["fields"]
661	    overflow = node.get("overflow")

671	                # name never seen before is still unexpected.
672	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
673	            else:

675	    for name, entry in fields.items():
676	        if name not in record:
677	            if not entry["optional"]:
678	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")

683	def _check_value(types: dict, value: Any, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
684	    kind = _kind_of(value)

697	# -- cross-revision compatibility -------------------------------------------
698	#
699	# Compatibility is read straight off the two committed schema trees, using
700	# exactly what ``check`` decides with: a record is accepted when every
701	# field it carries is a known (or genuinely overflow-folded) field whose
702	# value kind is in the entry's type set, every required field is present,
703	# and nested branches recurse. One symmetric walk therefore derives both
704	# directions at once: ``backward`` asks whether the new tree accepts every
705	# record the old tree accepts, ``forward`` the reverse.
706	#
707	# Each branch returns a ``(backward, forward)`` verdict pair. A branch
708	# either tree can only describe approximately - an overflow entry that may
709	# route the field, an entry flagged approximate, or a depth-capped subtree
710	# - is unknown in both directions and lists its source, in the same paths
711	# ``stats`` uses for approximated statistics (``$.*`` for an overflow
712	# entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). The one exception
713	# is comparing a revision with itself: that revision is known to accept its
714	# own records, so ``Lens.compat`` answers compatible in both directions
715	# with no reasons after the revision has been read and validated.
716	
717	_COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
718	_BREAKING = "breaking"
719	_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
720	
721	# Witness recipe step tags (see ``_CompatDiffer``): an object field
722	# descent, one array-element nesting, a forced-kind leaf, and an omission
723	# of the innermost field.
724	_FIELD = "f"
725	_ARRAY = "a"
726	_KIND = "k"
727	_MISSING = "m"

730	def _combine_pair(pair: tuple[str, str], other: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
731	    return (_worst(pair[0], other[0]), _worst(pair[1], other[1]))
732

734	def _worst(left: str, right: str) -> str:
735	    """Aggregate branch verdicts for one direction.
736	
737	    A branch that demonstrably rejects a legal record settles the
738	    direction as breaking even when another branch is unknowable; without
739	    one of those an unknown branch degrades it to unknown.
740	    """
741	    if left == _BREAKING or right == _BREAKING:
742	        return _BREAKING
743	    if left == _UNKNOWN or right == _UNKNOWN:
744	        return _UNKNOWN
745	    return _COMPATIBLE

749	    """Whether an overflow entry can route a field name during check.
750	
751	    An entry with known but empty provenance routes nothing; an explicit
752	    ``names: None`` (a pre-tracking overflow entry) routes any name.
753	    """
754	    names = entry.get("names", [])
755	    return names is None or bool(names)

758	def _overflow_routes(entry: dict | None, name: str) -> bool:
759	    if entry is None or not _overflow_live(entry):
760	        return False
761	    names = entry.get("names")
762	    return names is None or name in names

765	class _CompatDiffer:
766	    """Symmetric diff of two validated snapshots, aligned with ``check``."""
767	
768	    def __init__(self) -> None:
769	        self.changes: list[dict] = []
770	        self.reasons: set[str] = set()
771	        # One deterministic witness recipe per breaking pair position. Each
772	        # recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object to that
773	        # position, so a record can be built straight from a schema tree
774	        # without matching change strings, re-deriving the alignment, or
775	        # risking a collision between a real field name and a step token:
776	        # ``("f", name)`` descends through an object field, ``("a",)``
777	        # through one array element nesting, and the terminal step is
778	        # either ``("k", kind)`` (force a value of that kind) or
779	        # ``("m",)`` (omit the innermost field).
780	        self.recipes: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
781	        self._steps: list[tuple] = []
782	
783	    @contextlib.contextmanager
784	    def _step(self, step: tuple) -> Iterator[None]:
785	        self._steps.append(step)
786	        try:
787	            yield
788	        finally:
789	            self._steps.pop()
790	
791	    def witness(self, direction: str, terminal: tuple) -> None:
792	        """Record a witness recipe for one breaking pair position.
793	
794	        ``direction`` names the accepting (record) side for the breaking
795	        direction being witnessed (``"old"`` for a backward-breaking
796	        position, ``"new"`` for a forward-breaking one); ``terminal`` is
797	        the recipe's terminal step. Every call site is a non-collapsed
798	        exact branch the accepting side demonstrably accepts.
799	        """
800	        self.recipes.append((direction, tuple(self._steps) + (terminal,)))

802	    def diff(self, old_root: dict, new_root: dict) -> dict:
803	        backward, forward = self.compare_object(old_root, new_root, "$")
804	        self.changes.sort(key=lambda change: (change["path"], change["change"]))
805	        return {
806	            "backward": backward,
807	            "forward": forward,
808	            "changes": self.changes,
809	            "unknown_reasons": sorted(self.reasons),
810	        }

812	    def change(self, path: str, category: str, breaking: bool) -> None:
813	        self.changes.append(
814	            {"path": path, "change": category, "breaking": breaking}
815	        )

817	    def compare_object(self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
818	        if _is_collapsed(old) or _is_collapsed(new):
819	            # A depth-capped object lets anything nested through check, so
820	            # neither direction can be settled field by field.
821	            self.reasons.add(path)
822	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
823	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
824	        old_fields = old["fields"]
825	        new_fields = new["fields"]
826	        old_overflow = old.get("overflow")
827	        new_overflow = new.get("overflow")
828	        for name in sorted(set(old_fields) | set(new_fields)):
829	            field_path = _join(path, name)
830	            old_entry = old_fields.get(name)
831	            new_entry = new_fields.get(name)
832	            if old_entry is not None and new_entry is not None:
833	                with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
834	                    pair = self.compare_entry(old_entry, new_entry, field_path)
835	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
836	            elif old_entry is not None:
837	                # The field disappears from the new exact fields. New check
838	                # only accepts it when the name really folded into the new
839	                # overflow entry, whose merged type set is approximate.
840	                if _overflow_routes(new_overflow, name):
841	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
842	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
843	                else:
844	                    # New check rejects records carrying it; old records
845	                    # omitting it additionally fail an old required field
846	                    # under the forward direction.
847	                    self.change(field_path, "field_removed", True)
848	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
849	                        # A legal new record omits it; the old
850	                        # required-field check reports it missing. That
851	                        # witness needs no value kind.
852	                        if not old_entry["optional"]:
853	                            self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
854	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(old_entry)
855	                        if kind is not None:
856	                            # A legal old record carries the field; new
857	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
858	                            self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
859	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
860	                        verdict,
861	                        (_BREAKING,
862	                         _BREAKING if not old_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE),
863	                    )
864	            else:
865	                # The field appears only among the new exact fields. Old
866	                # check accepts it only through its own overflow entry.
867	                if _overflow_routes(old_overflow, name):
868	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
869	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
870	                else:
871	                    # Backward: an old record omits it, so a new required
872	                    # field rejects that record while a new optional one
873	                    # lets it through. Forward: old check calls any record
874	                    # carrying it unexpected.
875	                    self.change(
876	                        field_path, "field_added", not new_entry["optional"]
877	                    )
878	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
879	                        # A legal old record omits it; the new
880	                        # required-field check reports it missing.
881	                        if not new_entry["optional"]:
882	                            self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
883	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(new_entry)
884	                        if kind is not None:
885	                            # A legal new record carries the field; old
886	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
887	                            self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
888	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
889	                        verdict,
890	                        (_BREAKING if not new_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE,
891	                         _BREAKING),
892	                    )
893	        # A live overflow entry on either side folds names whose accepted
894	        # branches cannot be attributed exactly; every branch it governs is
895	        # unknown both ways. The marker can never be a real field name.
896	        for entry in (old_overflow, new_overflow):
897	            if entry is not None and _overflow_live(entry):
898	                self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
899	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
900	        return verdict

903	    def _witness_present_kind(entry: dict) -> str | None:

905	
906	        Exact field entries compared here are never approximate, and a
907	        validated entry has observed at least one record, so its type set
908	        is non-empty. The fixed kind order (null, boolean, number, string,
909	        array, object) makes the choice independent of dict iteration
910	        order; scalars are preferred and an array precedes an object.
911	        """
912	        for kind in _KINDS:
913	            if kind in entry["types"]:
914	                return kind
915	        return None

917	    def compare_entry(
918	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
919	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
920	        if old.get("approximate") or new.get("approximate"):
921	            # An entry flagged approximate absorbed overflow statistics in
922	            # an exact field position; its accepted value set cannot be
923	            # attributed precisely, so no change beneath it is asserted.
924	            self.reasons.add(path)
925	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
926	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
927	        if old["optional"] != new["optional"]:
928	            if old["optional"]:
929	                # Optional becomes required: old records may omit it. The
930	                # field name is the current innermost step; the missing
931	                # witness omits exactly that field.
932	                self.change(path, "optional_to_required", True)
933	                self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
934	                verdict = (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE)
935	            else:
936	                # Required becomes optional: new records may omit it.
937	                self.change(path, "required_to_optional", False)
938	                self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
939	                verdict = (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING)
940	        verdict = _combine_pair(
941	            verdict, self.compare_types(old["types"], new["types"], path, "type")

943	        return verdict

950	            if kind not in old_types and kind not in new_types:
951	                continue
952	            old_node = old_types.get(kind)
953	            new_node = new_types.get(kind)

962	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_removed", True)

969	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_added", False)

991	        even for a depth-capped array - only a collapsed *child* hides
992	        structure. So scalar element kinds gate exactly (rendered as
993	        ``path[]``) and collapsed element objects taint beneath them;
994	        element objects then join fields normally (``path[].name``). The
995	        matching array-level step marks the one nesting level check
996	        descends through per element.
997	        """

999	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
1000	        for kind in _KINDS:
1001	            if kind not in old["elements"] and kind not in new["elements"]:
1002	                continue
1003	            old_child = old["elements"].get(kind)
1004	            new_child = new["elements"].get(kind)
1005	            if old_child is not None and new_child is not None:
1006	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
1007	                    pair = self.compare_kind(old_child, new_child, element_path)
1008	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
1009	            elif old_child is not None:
1010	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_removed", True)

1029	# -- breaking-change witnesses ----------------------------------------------
1030	#
1031	# A witness for a breaking direction is one JSON object that the accepting
1032	# revision's ``check`` accepts (an empty report list) and the rejecting
1033	# revision's ``check`` rejects (the full, non-empty report list). The
1034	# differ records one recipe per breaking pair position while it walks; a
1035	# recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object, and the builder
1036	# below turns each into a concrete, deterministic record straight off the
1037	# accepting revision's tree - it never parses change strings and never
1038	# invents fields, kinds or values the accepting schema has not observed.
1039	# Required sibling fields are filled along the way so the record is legal
1040	# as a whole, not just at the breaking position; approximated branches are
1041	# never forced (a recipe can only end on a branch the differ proved), so
1042	# an ``unknown`` direction simply yields no witness.
1043	
1044	# Canonical, deterministic leaf values. Booleans and numbers stay
1045	# distinct kinds (``True`` is never used where a number is required), and
1046	# ``None`` is only produced for the explicit null kind, never for a
1047	# missing field.
1048	_WITNESS_VALUES = {
1049	    "null": None,
1050	    "boolean": True,
1051	    "number": 1,
1052	    "string": "x",
1053	}

1056	def _check_against(root: dict, record: Any) -> list[str]:
1057	    """Run the exact ``check`` pipeline against an in-memory root."""
1058	    reports: list[str] = []
1059	    if not isinstance(record, dict):
1060	        return [f"$: type {_kind_of(record)} not in field types [object]"]

1072	def _complete_value(types: dict, kind: str) -> Any:
1073	    """A deterministic value of ``kind`` legal under ``types``.
1074	
1075	    Scalars use canonical values; an object carries every required field
1076	    (each filled the same way); an array carries one complete element (or
1077	    stays empty when the schema tracked no element kinds - an empty array
1078	    passes check whatever the element type set).
1079	    """
1080	    if kind in _WITNESS_VALUES:
1081	        return _WITNESS_VALUES[kind]
1082	    node = types[kind]
1083	    if kind == "object":
1084	        return _complete_object(node)

1088	def _complete_object(node: dict) -> dict:

1090	        # A depth-capped object accepts anything, so the empty object is
1091	        # the smallest deterministic legal value.
1092	        return {}
1093	    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
1094	    for name in sorted(node["fields"]):
1095	        entry = node["fields"][name]
1096	        if entry["optional"]:
1097	            continue
1098	        kind = _first_kind(entry["types"])
1099	        if kind is not None:
1100	            record[name] = _complete_value(entry["types"], kind)
1101	    return record

1104	def _complete_array(node: dict) -> list:
1105	    kind = _first_kind(node["elements"])
1106	    if kind is None:
1107	        # No element kinds were ever observed (empty arrays folded here);
1108	        # check walks no elements, so the empty array passes.
1109	        return []
1110	    return [_complete_value(node["elements"], kind)]

1113	def _fill_required(node: dict, record: dict, skip: str | None) -> None:
1114	    """Add every still-missing required sibling field to ``record``."""
1115	    if _is_collapsed(node):
1116	        return
1117	    for name in sorted(node["fields"]):
1118	        if name == skip or name in record:
1119	            continue
1120	        entry = node["fields"][name]
1121	        if entry["optional"]:
1122	            continue
1123	        kind = _first_kind(entry["types"])
1124	        if kind is not None:
1125	            record[name] = _complete_value(entry["types"], kind)

1128	def _witness_value(types: dict, recipe: tuple, index: int) -> tuple[Any, int]:
1129	    """Build the value at one field/element position from ``recipe``.
1130	
1131	    ``types`` is the accepting side's type set at that position and
1132	    ``index`` points at the next step. Returns the value and the index of
1133	    the consumed terminal step.
1134	    """
1135	    tag, *payload = recipe[index]
1136	    if tag == _ARRAY:
1137	        # One nesting level: check walks every element against the one
1138	        # merged element set, so a single element witnesses the branch.
1139	        node = types["array"]
1140	        element, terminal = _witness_value(node["elements"], recipe, index + 1)
1141	        return [element], terminal
1142	    if tag == _FIELD:
1143	        node = types["object"]
1144	        return _witness_object_field(node, recipe, index)
1145	    # Terminal forced kind.
1146	    assert tag == _KIND
1147	    return _complete_value(types, payload[0]), index

1150	def _witness_object_field(
1151	    node: dict, recipe: tuple, index: int
1152	) -> tuple[Any, int]:
1153	    """Build an object value, forcing the recipe's field within it."""
1154	    tag, name = recipe[index]
1155	    assert tag == _FIELD
1156	    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
1157	    next_index = index + 1
1158	    next_step = recipe[next_index]
1159	    if next_step[0] == _MISSING:
1160	        # The witness omits this field, which the accepting tree may not
1161	        # even track (a field the other side removed or only it requires);
1162	        # only required siblings are filled.
1163	        _fill_required(node, record, name)
1164	        return record, next_index
1165	    entry = node["fields"][name]
1166	    value, terminal = _witness_value(entry["types"], recipe, next_index)
1167	    record[name] = value
1168	    _fill_required(node, record, name)
1169	    return record, terminal

1172	def _witness_record(root: dict, recipe: tuple) -> dict:
1173	    """Build the deterministic record one witness recipe describes."""
1174	    record, terminal = _witness_object_field(root, recipe, 0)
1175	    assert terminal == len(recipe) - 1
1176	    return record

1179	def _witness_report(
1180	    old_revision: int, new_revision: int, old_root: dict, new_root: dict
1181	) -> dict:
1182	    """The compat report plus verifiable breaking-direction witnesses."""
1183	    differ = _CompatDiffer()
1184	    report = differ.diff(old_root, new_root)
1185	    witnesses: dict[str, Any] = {"backward": None, "forward": None}
1186	    for direction, verdict, accepting, rejecting, side in (
1187	        ("backward", report["backward"], old_root, new_root, "old"),
1188	        ("forward", report["forward"], new_root, old_root, "new"),
1189	    ):
1190	        if verdict != _BREAKING:
1191	            # A compatible direction has no counterexample; an unknown
1192	            # direction cannot be settled, so one must never be forged.
1193	            continue
1194	        chosen: dict[str, Any] | None = None
1195	        for recipe_side, recipe in differ.recipes:
1196	            if recipe_side != side:
1197	                continue
1198	            record = _witness_record(accepting, recipe)
1199	            accepted_reports = _check_against(accepting, record)
1200	            rejected_reports = _check_against(rejecting, record)
1201	            if not accepted_reports and rejected_reports:
1202	                chosen = {"record": record, "reports": rejected_reports}
1203	                break

1205	        # pair position, whose recipe must verify through check itself.
1206	        if chosen is None:  # pragma: no cover - construction invariant
1207	            raise SchemaConflict("could not construct a verifiable witness")
1208	        witnesses[direction] = chosen
1209	    return {
1210	        "from": old_revision,
1211	        "to": new_revision,
1212	        **report,
1213	        "witnesses": witnesses,
1214	    }

1217	# -- field migration preview -------------------------------------------------
1218	#
1219	# A migration rule is a small JSON object describing one field-level edit:
1220	# ``{"op": "rename", "path": [...], "to": name}`` moves a field's value to
1221	# a new sibling name, ``{"op": "drop", "path": [...]}`` removes a field,
1222	# and ``{"op": "default", "path": [...], "value": ...}`` fills a field that
1223	# is genuinely missing (a present ``null`` is a value and is kept). The
1224	# path is a non-empty array whose string segments are literal field names
1225	# (a name containing a dot names one field, never a descent) and whose
1226	# ``null`` segments select every element of the array at that position;
1227	# the last segment is always a string naming the field the op edits.
1228	# Rules apply in order, each to the result of the previous one. A parent
1229	# that is simply missing skips the rule for that branch - parents are
1230	# never created - while a string segment meeting a non-object or a null
1231	# segment meeting a non-array is a structural ``ValueError``, as is a
1232	# rename whose target field already exists.
1233	
1234	_MIGRATION_OPS = ("rename", "drop", "default")
1235	
1236	
1237	def _require_json_value(value: Any, what: str) -> None:
1238	    """Reject anything JSON cannot represent, recursing into containers."""
1239	    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
1240	        return
1241	    if isinstance(value, float):
1242	        if math.isfinite(value):
1243	            return
1244	    elif isinstance(value, list):
1245	        for item in value:
1246	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1247	        return
1248	    elif isinstance(value, dict):
1249	        for key, item in value.items():
1250	            if not isinstance(key, str):
1251	                break
1252	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1253	        else:
1254	            return
1255	    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be a JSON value")

1258	def _parse_migration_rules(rules: Any, *, label: str = "migration rule") -> list[dict]:
1259	    """Validate the rule list structurally before anything is applied.
1260	
1261	    Every rule must be a JSON object carrying exactly the keys its op
1262	    needs - ``op`` and ``path`` for all three, ``to`` for rename,
1263	    ``value`` for default - with a non-empty path of string/null segments
1264	    ending in a string, a string rename target distinct from the source
1265	    field name, and a JSON default value. Anything else is a
1266	    ``ValueError`` raised before any revision is read or any rule runs.
1267	    ``label`` names the group in error messages so forward and rollback
1268	    rules are distinguishable in a roundtrip preview.
1269	    """
1270	    if not isinstance(rules, list):
1271	        raise ValueError(f"{label}s must be a JSON array")
1272	    for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
1273	        if not isinstance(rule, dict):
1274	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index} must be a JSON object")
1275	        op = rule.get("op")
1276	        if op not in _MIGRATION_OPS:
1277	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: unknown op {op!r}")
1278	        path = rule.get("path")
1279	        if (
1280	            not isinstance(path, list)
1281	            or not path
1282	            or any(
1283	                segment is not None and not isinstance(segment, str)
1284	                for segment in path
1285	            )
1286	            or not isinstance(path[-1], str)
1287	        ):
1288	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: invalid path")
1289	        expected = {"op", "path"}
1290	        if op == "rename":
1291	            expected.add("to")
1292	        elif op == "default":
1293	            expected.add("value")
1294	        if set(rule) != expected:
1295	            raise ValueError(f"{label} {index}: invalid keys for {op}")
1296	        if op == "rename":
1297	            if not isinstance(rule["to"], str):
1298	                raise ValueError(
1299	                    f"{label} {index}: rename target must be a string"
1300	                )
1301	            if rule["to"] == path[-1]:
1302	                raise ValueError(
1303	                    f"{label} {index}: rename target equals the "
1304	                    "source field"
1305	                )
1306	        elif op == "default":
1307	            _require_json_value(rule["value"], f"{label} {index} value")
1308	    return rules

1311	def _migration_containers(record: dict, path: list) -> list:
1312	    """The containers the path's final segment applies to.
1313	
1314	    Navigates every segment but the last: a string segment descends into
1315	    the named field of an object (a missing field drops that branch
1316	    silently - parents are never created), a null segment spreads over
1317	    every element of an array (an empty array simply selects nothing).
1318	    A string segment meeting a non-object or a null segment meeting a
1319	    non-array is a structural ``ValueError``.
1320	    """
1321	    containers = [record]
1322	    for segment in path[:-1]:
1323	        following = []
1324	        for container in containers:
1325	            if segment is None:
1326	                if not isinstance(container, list):
1327	                    raise ValueError("null path segment requires an array")
1328	                following.extend(container)
1329	            else:
1330	                if not isinstance(container, dict):
1331	                    raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1332	                if segment in container:
1333	                    following.append(container[segment])
1334	        if not following:
1335	            return []
1336	        containers = following
1337	    return containers

1340	def _apply_migration_rule(record: dict, rule: dict) -> None:
1341	    """Apply one already-validated rule to the working record in place."""
1342	    op = rule["op"]
1343	    last = rule["path"][-1]
1344	    for container in _migration_containers(record, rule["path"]):
1345	        if not isinstance(container, dict):
1346	            raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1347	        if op == "rename":
1348	            if last not in container:
1349	                continue
1350	            to = rule["to"]
1351	            if to in container:
1352	                raise ValueError(f"rename target {to!r} already exists")
1353	            # Rebuild in place so the field keeps its position under the
1354	            # new name and the same input always yields the same order.
1355	            renamed = [
1356	                (to if key == last else key, value)
1357	                for key, value in container.items()
1358	            ]
1359	            container.clear()
1360	            container.update(renamed)
1361	        elif op == "drop":
1362	            container.pop(last, None)
1363	        # default fills only a genuinely missing field; a present null is
1364	        # a value and is never replaced.
1365	        elif last not in container:
1366	            container[last] = copy.deepcopy(rule["value"])

1369	# -- rollback rehearsal ------------------------------------------------------
1370	#
1371	# After the forward migration preview succeeds, the rollback rules run on
1372	# the migrated record and the recovered object is checked against the old
1373	# revision and then compared structurally with the original record. The
1374	# comparison ignores object key order and compares objects key by key;
1375	# arrays of the same length compare element by element. A missing key
1376	# records that field's path; a type mismatch, an unequal array length or
1377	# unequal scalars record only the current position and never expand it.
1378	# Missing is distinct from null and booleans are distinct from numbers,
1379	# while ints and floats compare by numeric value. Paths reuse the check
1380	# field/array notation (``_join``) and are reported de-duplicated in
1381	# string order.

1384	def _json_kind(value: Any) -> str:
1385	    """The comparison kind, splitting booleans off from numbers."""
1386	    if value is None:
1387	        return "null"
1388	    if isinstance(value, bool):
1389	        return "boolean"
1390	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
1391	        return "number"
1392	    if isinstance(value, str):
1393	        return "string"
1394	    if isinstance(value, list):
1395	        return "array"
1396	    return "object"

1399	def _scalars_equal(left: Any, right: Any) -> bool:
1400	    """Scalar equality with ints and floats compared by numeric value."""
1401	    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
1402	        return left is right
1403	    return left == right

1406	def _structural_differences(original: Any, recovered: Any, path: str) -> list[str]:
1407	    """Every path at which two JSON values differ, check path notation."""
1408	    left_kind = _json_kind(original)
1409	    right_kind = _json_kind(recovered)
1410	    if left_kind != right_kind:
1411	        # A type difference (missing vs null, boolean vs number included)
1412	        # is terminal at the current position.
1413	        return [path]
1414	    if left_kind == "object":
1415	        differences: list[str] = []
1416	        for name in sorted(set(original) | set(recovered)):
1417	            field_path = _join(path, name)
1418	            if name not in original or name not in recovered:
1419	                # A key one side lacks names exactly that field path.
1420	                differences.append(field_path)
1421	            else:
1422	                differences.extend(
1423	                    _structural_differences(
1424	                        original[name], recovered[name], field_path
1425	                    )
1426	                )
1427	        return differences
1428	    if left_kind == "array":
1429	        if len(original) != len(recovered):
1430	            return [path]
1431	        differences = []
1432	        for index, (left_element, right_element) in enumerate(
1433	            zip(original, recovered)
1434	        ):
1435	            differences.extend(
1436	                _structural_differences(
1437	                    left_element, right_element, f"{path}[{index}]"
1438	                )
1439	            )
1440	        return differences
1441	    if _scalars_equal(original, recovered):
1442	        return []
1443	    return [path]

1446	def _structural_diff_paths(original: dict, recovered: dict) -> list[str]:

1561	def _normalize_overflow_names(node: Any) -> None:
1562	    """Mark pre-tracking overflow entries with explicit ``names: None``.
1563	
1564	    Files written before folded names were tracked carry overflow entries
1565	    without a ``names`` key; unlike an exact entry (which also omits the
1566	    key), their provenance is unknown and must stay permissive through
1567	    merges. Exact entries are never reached here.
1568	    """

1570	        return
1571	    kind = node.get("kind")
1572	    if kind == "object" and not _is_collapsed(node):
1573	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
1574	        if overflow is not None and "names" not in overflow:
1575	            overflow["names"] = None
1576	        fields = node.get("fields") or {}
1577	        for entry in fields.values():
1578	            for child in (entry.get("types") or {}).values():
1579	                _normalize_overflow_names(child)
1580	        if overflow is not None:
1581	            for child in (overflow.get("types") or {}).values():
